description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\) and \(Q = \text{False}\), what is \((P \leftrightarrow Q) \leftrightarrow (P \rightarrow Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(P \leftrightarrow Q\) is False; \(P \rightarrow Q\) is False; \((P \leftrightarrow Q) \leftrightarrow (P \rightarrow Q)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(X = \text{True}\) and \(Y = \text{False}\), what is \((X \leftrightarrow Y) \leftrightarrow (X \land Y)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(X \leftrightarrow Y\) is False; \(X \land Y\) is False; \((X \leftrightarrow Y) \leftrightarrow (X \land Y)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(A = \text{False}\) and \(B = \text{True}\), what is \((A \rightarrow B) \lor (A \rightarrow B)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(A \rightarrow B\) is True; \(A \rightarrow B\) is True; \((A \rightarrow B) \lor (A \rightarrow B)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a disjunction with a negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{False}\) and \(Q = \text{True}\), what is \((P \land Q) \lor (P \leftrightarrow Q)\)?

questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\) and \(Q = \text{False}\), what is \((P \land Q) \leftrightarrow (P \leftrightarrow Q)\)?

questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a disjunction with a negation.

questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(A = \text{False}\) and \(B = \text{True}\), what is \((A \rightarrow B) \leftrightarrow (A \land B)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(A \rightarrow B\) is True; \(A \land B\) is False; \((A \rightarrow B) \leftrightarrow (A \land B)\) is False. Therefore the result is False.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a conjunction with a negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\) and \(Q = \text{False}\), what is \(P \land \neg Q\)?
questions.explanation: \(\neg Q = \text{True}\), so \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Negate \(Q\) first, then apply AND.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a tautology with a negation.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{True}\), what is \(\neg X \lor X\)?
questions.explanation: \(\neg X = \text{False}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{False}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \((P \lor Q) \lor R\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(P \lor Q\) is True; \((P \lor Q) \lor R\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \((P \leftrightarrow Q) \rightarrow R\)?

questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{False}\), and \(C = \text{True}\), what is \((A \lor B) \land C\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \lor B = \text{True}\), then \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the OR inside parentheses first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{False}\), \(Y = \text{True}\), and \(Z = \text{False}\), what is \(Z \lor (X \rightarrow Y)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(X \rightarrow Y\) is True; \(Z \lor (X \rightarrow Y)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \(P \land (Q \lor R)\)?
questions.explanation: \(Q \lor R = \text{True}\), then \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the OR inside parentheses first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with parentheses.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{True}\), and \(C = \text{False}\), what is \((A \leftrightarrow B) \leftrightarrow C\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(A \leftrightarrow B\) is True; \((A \leftrightarrow B) \leftrightarrow C\) is False. Therefore the result is False.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), and \(R = \text{True}\), what is \(P \lor Q \land R\)?
questions.explanation: AND is evaluated first: \(Q \land R = \text{False}\). Then \(P \lor \text{False} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Remember that AND has higher precedence than OR.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{False}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \(P \lor Q \land R\)?
questions.explanation: \(Q \land R = \text{False}\), then \(P \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the AND part before the OR.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{False}\), and \(C = \text{True}\), what is \(\neg A \lor (B \land C)\)?
questions.explanation: \(\neg A = \text{False}\), \(B \land C = \text{False}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the negation and parentheses first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{True}\), \(Y = \text{False}\), and \(Z = \text{False}\), what is \(\neg(X \lor Y) \land Z\)?
questions.explanation: \(X \lor Y = \text{True}\), \(\neg(\text{True}) = \text{False}\), then \(\text{False} \land \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the parentheses, then negate, then apply AND.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.

questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{True}\), and \(C = \text{False}\), what is \(\neg(A \land B) \lor C\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \land B = \text{True}\), \(\neg(\text{True}) = \text{False}\), then \(\text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the parentheses, then negate, then apply OR.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \(\neg P \lor (Q \land R)\)?
questions.explanation: \(\neg P = \text{False}\), \(Q \land R = \text{False}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the negation and parentheses first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{False}\), \(Y = \text{True}\), and \(Z = \text{False}\), what is \((X \lor Y) \land \neg Z\)?
questions.explanation: \(X \lor Y = \text{True}\), \(\neg Z = \text{True}\), then \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the parentheses and the negation first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{True}\), what is \((P \land \neg Q) \lor R\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \land \neg Q = \text{True} \land \text{False} = \text{False}\), then \(\text{False} \lor \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the negation, then the conjunction, then OR.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{False}\), \(B = \text{False}\), and \(C = \text{True}\), what is \((A \lor B) \land \neg C\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \lor B = \text{False}\), \(\neg C = \text{False}\), then \(\text{False} \land \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the parentheses and negation first.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \(\neg(P \land Q) \lor R\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \land Q = \text{False}\), \(\neg(\text{False}) = \text{True}\), then \(\text{True} \lor \text{False} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the conjunction, negate it, then apply OR.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{True}\), \(Y = \text{True}\), and \(Z = \text{False}\), what is \(\neg(X \lor Y) \land (Y \lor Z)\)?
questions.explanation: \(X \lor Y = \text{True}\), \(\neg(\text{True}) = \text{False}\), \(Y \lor Z = \text{True}\), then \(\text{False} \land \text{True} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{False}\), \(B = \text{True}\), and \(C = \text{True}\), what is \((A \land B) \lor (\neg B \land C)\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \land B = \text{False}\), \(\neg B \land C = \text{False} \land \text{True} = \text{False}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each conjunction separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{False}\), what is \((P \lor Q) \land (\neg Q \lor R)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \lor Q = \text{True}\), \(\neg Q \lor R = \text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\), so \(\text{True} \land \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with disjunction.
questions.question: If \(X = \text{False}\), \(Y = \text{True}\), and \(Z = \text{True}\), what is \((X \lor Y) \land (Y \lor Z)\)?
questions.explanation: \(X \lor Y = \text{True}\), \(Y \lor Z = \text{True}\), so \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), and \(R = \text{True}\), what is \((P \land Q) \lor (\neg P \land R)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \land Q = \text{False}\), \(\neg P \land R = \text{False} \land \text{True} = \text{False}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{False} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each conjunction separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{False}\), and \(C = \text{True}\), what is \(A \lor (B \land \neg C)\)?
questions.explanation: \(B \land \neg C = \text{False} \land \text{False} = \text{False}\), then \(\text{True} \lor \text{False} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the negation and conjunction first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression with negation.
questions.question: If \(P = \text{False}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), and \(R = \text{True}\), what is \(\neg(P \lor Q) \lor (Q \land R)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \lor Q = \text{True}\), \(\neg(\text{True}) = \text{False}\), \(Q \land R = \text{True}\), so \(\text{False} \lor \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each part separately.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), \(R = \text{True}\), and \(S = \text{False}\), what is \((P \lor Q) \land (R \lor S)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \lor Q = \text{True}\), \(R \lor S = \text{True}\), so \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{False}\), \(C = \text{True}\), and \(D = \text{False}\), what is \((A \land \neg B) \lor (C \land \neg D)\)?
questions.explanation: \(A \land \neg B = \text{True}\), \(C \land \neg D = \text{True}\), so \(\text{True} \lor \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each conjunction separately.

questions.question: If \(X = \text{False}\), \(Y = \text{True}\), \(Z = \text{True}\), and \(W = \text{False}\), what is \((X \lor Y) \land (Z \lor W)\)?
questions.explanation: \(X \lor Y = \text{True}\), \(Z \lor W = \text{True}\), so \(\text{True} \land \text{True} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{True}\), \(Q = \text{True}\), \(R = \text{False}\), and \(S = \text{False}\), what is \((P \land Q) \lor (R \land S)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \land Q = \text{True}\), \(R \land S = \text{False}\), so \(\text{True} \lor \text{False} = \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each conjunction separately.

questions.question: If \(A = \text{True}\), \(B = \text{False}\), \(C = \text{True}\), and \(D = \text{False}\), what is \((A \leftrightarrow B) \leftrightarrow (C \leftrightarrow D)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(A \leftrightarrow B\) is False; \(C \leftrightarrow D\) is False; \((A \leftrightarrow B) \leftrightarrow (C \leftrightarrow D)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.question: If \(P = \text{False}\), \(Q = \text{False}\), \(R = \text{True}\), and \(S = \text{True}\), what is \((P \lor Q) \land (R \lor S)\)?
questions.explanation: \(P \lor Q = \text{False}\), \(R \lor S = \text{True}\), so \(\text{False} \land \text{True} = \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each parenthesized part separately.

questions.learningObjective: Apply De Morgan's law to a conjunction.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((\neg P \land Q) \lor (P \land Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Factor out \(Q\): \((\neg P \lor P) \land Q \equiv \text{True} \land Q \equiv Q\).
questions.hint: Look for a common factor, a double negation, or the equivalence \(A \rightarrow B \equiv \neg A \lor B\).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(\neg(\neg P)\)?
questions.explanation: Double negation cancels: \(\neg(\neg P) \equiv P\).
questions.hint: Two NOT operations cancel each other.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the identity law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land \text{True}\)?
questions.explanation: Identity law: \(P \land \text{True} \equiv P\).
questions.hint: AND with True does not change the other operand.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the identity law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor \text{False}\)?
questions.explanation: Identity law: \(P \lor \text{False} \equiv P\).
questions.hint: OR with False does not change the other operand.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the domination law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land \text{False}\)?
questions.explanation: Domination law: \(P \land \text{False} \equiv \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the domination law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor \text{True}\)?
questions.explanation: Domination law: \(P \lor \text{True} \equiv \text{True}\).
questions.hint: OR with True always gives True.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the idempotent law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land P\)?
questions.explanation: Idempotent law: \(P \land P \equiv P\).
questions.hint: Repeating a condition with AND does not change it.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the idempotent law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor P\)?
questions.explanation: Idempotent law: \(P \lor P \equiv P\).
questions.hint: Repeating a condition with OR does not change it.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the complement law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land \neg P\)?
questions.explanation: Complement law: \(P \land \neg P \equiv \text{False}\).
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the complement law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor \neg P\)?
questions.explanation: Complement law: \(P \lor \neg P \equiv \text{True}\).
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the commutative law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land Q\)?
questions.explanation: Commutative law: \(P \land Q \equiv Q \land P\).
questions.hint: Order does not matter for AND.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the commutative law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor Q\)?
questions.explanation: Commutative law: \(P \lor Q \equiv Q \lor P\).
questions.hint: Order does not matter for OR.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the associative law for AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((P \land Q) \land R\)?
questions.explanation: Associative law: \((P \land Q) \land R \equiv P \land (Q \land R)\).
questions.hint: Grouping does not matter for AND.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the associative law for OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((P \lor Q) \lor R\)?
questions.explanation: Associative law: \((P \lor Q) \lor R \equiv P \lor (Q \lor R)\).
questions.hint: Grouping does not matter for OR.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the distributive law of AND over OR.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land (Q \lor R)\)?
questions.explanation: Distributive law: \(P \land (Q \lor R) \equiv (P \land Q) \lor (P \land R)\).
questions.hint: Distribute \(P\) over each term inside the parentheses.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the distributive law of OR over AND.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor (Q \land R)\)?
questions.explanation: Distributive law: \(P \lor (Q \land R) \equiv (P \lor Q) \land (P \lor R)\).
questions.hint: Distribute \(P\) over each term using OR.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor (P \land Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Absorption law: \(P \lor (P \land Q) \equiv P\).
questions.hint: The term \(P \land Q\) is absorbed by \(P\).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land (P \lor Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Absorption law: \(P \land (P \lor Q) \equiv P\).
questions.hint: The term \(P \lor Q\) is absorbed by \(P\).

questions.learningObjective: Apply a combined distributive and complement law.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor (\neg P \land Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Distribute: \((P \lor \neg P) \land (P \lor Q) \equiv \text{True} \land (P \lor Q) \equiv P \lor Q\).
questions.hint: Use the distributive law and then \(P \lor \neg P \equiv \text{True}\).

questions.learningObjective: Apply a combined distributive and complement law.
questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \land (\neg P \lor Q)\)?
questions.explanation: Distribute: \((P \land \neg P) \lor (P \land Q) \equiv \text{False} \lor (P \land Q) \equiv P \land Q\).
questions.hint: Use the distributive law and then \(P \land \neg P \equiv \text{False}\).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((P \land Q) \lor (P \land R)\)?
questions.explanation: Factor \(P\): \((P \land Q) \lor (P \land R) \equiv P \land (Q \lor R)\).
questions.hint: Factor out the common term \(P\).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \((P \lor Q) \land (P \lor R)\)?
questions.explanation: Factor \(P\): \((P \lor Q) \land (P \lor R) \equiv P \lor (Q \land R)\).
questions.hint: Factor out the common term \(P\).

questions.explanation: Associativity allows grouping as \((P \land Q) \land R\).
questions.hint: AND expressions can be regrouped without changing meaning.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to \(P \lor Q \lor R\)?
questions.explanation: Associativity allows grouping as \((P \lor Q) \lor R\).
questions.hint: OR expressions can be regrouped without changing meaning.
